relationships.subject: protoxin-II
relationships.evidence_quote: Our simulations revealed that PTx2 binds most favorably to the deactivated VSD II and activated VSD IV.

relationships.subject: protoxin-II
relationships.evidence_quote: The tarantula venom peptide protoxin-II (PTx2) has high selectivity for hNaV1.7 and is a valuable scaffold for designing novel therapeutics to treat pain.

relationships.subject: protoxin-II
relationships.evidence_quote: Previously, it was determined that PTx2 interferes with NaV1.7 activation by binding potently (IC50 = 0.3–1.0 nM) to the S3–S4 loop in VSD II and shifting the voltage dependence of activation to more depolarized potentials

relationships.subject: protoxin-II
relationships.evidence_quote: Experimental results show that PTx2 can also bind to NaV1.7 VSD IV and modulate channel inactivation (Xiao et al., 2010), although with much lower potency (IC50 = 0.24 μM).

key_findings: MD simulations and MM/PBSA show PTx2 binds most favorably to the deactivated VSD II of hNaV1.7 (-23.1 kcal/mol), matching electrophysiological state dependence.
State-specific binding is mediated by PTx2 residues R22, K26, K27, K28 and W30 contacting VSD residues of the S3-S4 loop and surrounding membrane lipids.
